dtFaq.q: How long does a LIDAR scan-to-twin take in Anchorage?
dtFaq.a: A mid-sized refinery scan runs five to ten field days, then two to four weeks of registration and clean-up before the twin goes live.

dtFaq.q: Which IoT sensor protocols does the Anchorage twin ingest?

dtFaq.q: How is NDT data overlaid onto the Anchorage twin?

dtFaq.q: Does the Anchorage twin feed API 580/581 RBI calculations?
dtFaq.a: Yes. Thickness, temperature, pressure and inspection-effectiveness flow into API 580/581 models. Re-inspection intervals replan as new data lands.

dtFaq.q: Can Atlantis deliver the Anchorage digital twin fully remote?
dtFaq.a: Yes. The customer's scan crew works in Anchorage; Atlantis handles registration, IoT tag mapping, and NDT overlay Level III sign-off over secure VPN.

dtFaq.q: How does the Anchorage twin connect to existing ERP or CMMS?
dtFaq.a: Pre-built connectors push twin-driven work orders into SAP PM, IBM Maximo and Meridium/APM, and pull asset master data back one traceable loop.
